Well, they told me I had to come see you because... my talking gets all mixed up, I guess. Like, I was just trying to explain to my boss about the keys for the supply closets. Heavy brass keys, you know? They clink together just like the ones down at the jail. I knew a guy in jail once who carved little birds out of soap, real detailed work... but anyway, I try to tell 'em about the keys, and the jail, and then the prayer rug I found. I always like playing the knights, they move different than the rest... but when I try to lay it all out for people, how the keys and the rug and the chess pieces all go together, they just stop me. They tell me they can't follow what I'm saying at all. So... I guess that's why I'm here.

Yeah, sleep just... it just goes out the window. I can sleep two or three hours, tops, and I get up before dawn feeling completely fresh. It's like sleep is something other people need, not me. I just start planning out all my work, getting everything lined up.

Yeah, I definitely get those... those really bad spells. On my bad days, I just sit on the edge of the bed after my morning prayer, and I feel so heavy. Just empty inside. Like there's no point in even cleaning myself up or going outside. 

It's hard to explain that heaviness. It feels like you're wearing wet clothes. Have you ever been caught in a really sudden downpour? We had one of those last spring. I was walking back from the corner store with a gallon of milk, and the sky just opened up. Completely soaked me to the bone in seconds. The plastic bag broke, too. They make those bags so thin now. You try to carry anything heavier than a loaf of bread and the handles just stretch right out until they snap. I miss the old paper bags. They had that nice thick brown paper. You could use them to cover your textbooks in school. We used to do that back in junior high. We'd fold the paper bags over the covers and draw all over them with ballpoint pens. I used to draw cars. Big muscle cars with flames on the side. I wanted a Camaro so bad back then. A 1969 Camaro RS, cherry red with the white racing stripes. My buddy Jimmy's older brother had one, and he'd let us sit in it sometimes if we promised not to touch the radio. The radio had these little silver knobs that clicked when you turned them. You don't see knobs like that anymore, everything is all digital and touch screens now. You tap the screen and half the time it doesn't even register your finger. My phone does that. I have to tap the screen three times just to answer a call...

But yeah, the depression. It gets really bad for weeks at a time. I just sit there feeling completely empty, like nothing matters.

Because I swear you just asked me this exact same thing a few minutes ago. We keep going in circles here. But yeah, I'll say it again. There have definitely been calmer weeks where I wasn't especially high, and I wasn't deeply depressed either. Just totally normal. But even then, for more than two weeks at a time, I still heard the man in the vents, and I still believed the people in the building were signaling about me. \n\nSpeaking of circles, they have this big glass revolving door down in the main lobby of the building. I absolutely hate cleaning the glass on that thing. People are supposed to push the metal bar, right? That's what it's there for. But they don't. They put their bare hands right on the glass and leave these big oily handprints. Kids are the absolute worst for it. They just smear their sticky little fingers everywhere. I don't even know what kids eat nowadays to get their hands so sticky all the time. Probably those gummy fruit snacks. My sister used to buy those huge bulk boxes of them for her kids. They're shaped like little dinosaurs or sharks or something, but they just taste like wax and cherry syrup. You gotta watch out for that red dye, too. Red dye number 40. I saw a show on public television that said it makes kids bounce off the walls. I like watching public television late at night. They have those old British shows where everyone lives in a big manor house and drinks tea. They always have very nice teacups, the kind with the little matching saucers... \n\nBut, anyway, yeah. My mood can be totally normal for a couple weeks, but the vent guy and the signals are still happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I definitely get those... those really bad spells. On my bad days, I just sit on the edge of the bed after my morning prayer, and I feel so heavy. Just empty inside. Big muscle cars with flames on the side. I wanted a Camaro so bad back then. A 1969 Camaro RS, cherry red with the white racing stripes. My buddy Jimmy's older brother had one, and he'd let us sit in it sometimes if we promised not to touch the radio. The radio had these little silver knobs that clicked when you turned them. You don't see knobs like that anymore, everything is all digital and touch screens now. You tap the screen and half the time it doesn't even register your finger. My phone does that. I have to tap the screen three times just to answer a call...\n\nBut yeah, the depression. It gets really bad for weeks at a time. Sometimes I just feel so... so powerful, you know? Like I'm on top of the world. I'll be laughing, talking real loud to everybody in the building, just feeling completely unstoppable. I'll start shouting over the smallest little thing. \n\nLike this one time, this guy on the third floor asked me why I was mopping the hallway twice. I just lost it on him. I told him he didn't know the first thing about floor maintenance. Floor maintenance is a real art, you know? You have to use the right ratio of cleaner to water. If you use too much soap, it leaves a film. A sticky film that catches all the dust and dirt from people's shoes. And people wear the worst shoes for floors. Those heavy work boots with the deep treads? They track in mud, salt in the winter... rock salt is terrible for linoleum. It scratches the finish right off. You have to strip it and re-wax it, and that takes hours. You need one of those big rotary floor buffers. The ones that weigh like a hundred pounds. You have to swing it side to side, from your hips. I'll start shouting over the smallest little thing. \n\nLike this one time, this guy on the third floor asked me why I was mopping the hallway twice. I just lost it on him. I told him he didn't know the first thing about floor maintenance. Floor maintenance is a real art, you know? You have to use the right ratio of cleaner to water. If you use too much soap, it leaves a film. A sticky film that catches all the dust and dirt from people's shoes. And people wear the worst shoes for floors. Those heavy work boots with the deep treads? They track in mud, salt in the winter... rock salt is terrible for linoleum. It scratches the finish right off. You have to strip it and re-wax it, and that takes hours. You need one of those big rotary floor buffers. The ones that weigh like a hundred pounds. You have to swing it side to side, from your hips. It's a real workout. My buddy used to work at a bowling alley, and he said buffing the lanes was even harder. They use this special oil on bowling lanes. Did you know that? They oil the lanes so the ball hooks right. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. We had these matching shirts, bright green with our names embroidered on the pocket. My name was stitched in this yellow thread that started unraveling after three washes. You can't find good embroidery anymore. Everything is just screen-printed now, and the print cracks and peels off in the dryer...\n\nBut yeah, I get really energized and loud, and if somebody gets in my way, I just explode on them. It definitely gets me into trouble.\n\nDoctor: Have there been any times when the voices or beliefs were present only during your mood episodes and completely went away when your mood was back to normal?\n\nPatient: Well, no, it's not like they completely go away when my mood is normal. I told you, I still hear the guy in the vents even on my calm weeks. But... yeah, when my mood is all over the place, the voices and the signals are definitely there too. Like, when I get into those states where I'm only sleeping a couple of hours a night and I'm drawing up all these big master plans to completely reorganize the building's maintenance schedule... during those times, the vent voice is right there with me, and I feel absolutely sure the hallway lights flickering are sending out warnings about me. \n\nSpeaking of the hallway lights, they use these cheap fluorescent tubes now. The ballasts go bad all the time, and they just hum. It's this low, constant buzzing sound that drives you crazy if you stand under it too long. And they give off this awful greenish light that makes everybody look sick. I remember when buildings used to have real incandescent bulbs. They had that warm, yellow glow. Made things look cozy. My grandmother had this big floor lamp in her living room with a fringed shade. It was real heavy, made of brass, I think. She kept it right next to her reading chair. She used to read these thick romance novels, the ones with the painted covers where the guy always has his shirt ripped open. She'd get them by the dozen from the used bookstore downtown. That bookstore smelled like old paper and dust. They had a cat that just slept on the counter all day. A big orange tabby. I had an orange cat once, named Marmalade. He used to bring dead mice and leave them right on the welcome mat. You'd step out in the morning and nearly squish them. Mice are a huge problem in older buildings, you know. They get into the walls and chew through the wiring. That's a huge fire hazard. You have to put down traps, but the snap traps are messy, and the glue traps just seem cruel...\n\nBut yeah, when I'm all wired and making those big plans, the vent guy and the light warnings are definitely happening at the same time.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had hallucinations or delusional beliefs when you were not having a mood episode, such as a manic or depressive episode?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. Like I was saying before, there are plenty of times when I'm just... regular. You know? Not stuck in bed feeling depressed, and not all fired up and yelling at people. Just a normal, calm mood. But even during those calm stretches, for like two or three weeks at a time, I still hear the man in the vents plain as day. And I still know people in the building are signaling about me. \n\nIt's especially loud when I'm working near the main intake grates in the hallways. Those grates are massive. You wouldn't believe the amount of dust that gets sucked into those things. Management is supposed to order the good pleated filters, the thick ones, but they always cheap out and buy those flimsy blue fiberglass ones. They don't catch a damn thing. All the dust just blows right through the system and settles right back down on the baseboards. I swear I spend half my life wiping down baseboards. You can't just use a dry duster, either, or it just kicks the dirt right back into the air. You gotta use a damp rag. We used to use old cut-up t-shirts for rags when I was growing up. My mom kept a whole drawer of them under the kitchen counter. That drawer always got stuck in the summer when it was humid. The wood swells up, you know? You have to take a bar of soap and rub it along the wooden runners to make it glide smooth again. Plain old bar soap. Ivory works the best for that. Did you know Ivory soap floats? I dropped a bar in the bathtub when I was maybe eight years old, and it just bobbed right there on the top of the water. We only got to take real baths on Sunday nights before the school week started. You had to make sure you scrubbed behind your ears, or the teacher would send you to the nurse's office to get checked for lice...\n\nDoctor: Have the voices or beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?\n\nPatient: Yeah, like I was just saying, I have those calm stretches. I'll have those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high or deeply depressed, just... regular, you know? But yeah, it's definitely been for more than two weeks at a time during those calm periods where I still hear the man in the vents every single day, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just go away because my mood is normal. \n\nTwo weeks is a long time to deal with that. Actually, two weeks is exactly how long management made us wait for a new fan belt for the rooftop AC unit last August. Two whole weeks! You wouldn't believe how hot the top floor gets when the air goes out. It's like an oven up there. The tenants were complaining to me non-stop, leaving sticky notes on my utility cart. They think I can just magically fix it, but I don't carry commercial fan belts in my back pocket. You have to order those from a specialty supply house. \n\nAnd the supply houses aren't like they used to be, let me tell you. Used to be you could just drive down to the industrial park on 4th street and pick up whatever you needed. There was this guy there, Sal, who knew every part number by heart. He didn't even need to look at a computer. Computers ruin everything, if you ask me. Everything is automated now. You call a number and get a robot voice telling you to press one for sales, press two for service. My sister got locked out of her bank account last month because she couldn't get past the robot on the phone. She just wanted to check her balance, but it kept asking her for a PIN she forgot. She had to drive all the way down to the physical branch, and the parking there is an absolute nightmare. They have those tiny spots that barely fit a compact car, let alone her big station wagon. It's a real boat of a car, one of those old ones with the fake wood paneling on the side. You don't see cars like that anymore. Now they all look like jellybeans. Just round and silver or white. Nobody buys a green or a blue car anymore... \n\nBut yeah, even when my mood is totally fine for over two weeks, the vent guy is still talking and the signals are still happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you heard voices or believed people were sending you messages while you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?\n\nPatient: Didn't we... It doesn't stop just 'cause my mood is fine. \n\nTwo weeks... you know, speaking of two weeks, that's usually how long you have to wait to get any kind of doctor's appointment anywhere these days anyway. Actually, it's worse now. I tried to get in to see the dentist last month because my lower bridge was aching. Just a dull throb, right where the gum meets the metal. My buddy Jimmy's older brother had one, and he'd let us sit in it sometimes if we promised not to touch the radio. The radio had these little silver knobs that clicked when you turned them. It's a real workout. My buddy used to work at a bowling alley, and he said buffing the lanes was even harder. They use this special oil on bowling lanes. Did you know that? They oil the lanes so the ball hooks right. I used to bowl in a league on Thursday nights. We had these matching shirts, bright green with our names embroidered on the pocket. My name was stitched in this yellow thread that started unraveling after three washes. You can't find good embroidery anymore. Everything is just screen-printed now, and the print cracks and peels off in the dryer...\n\nBut yeah, I get really energized and loud, and if somebody gets in my way, I just explode on them. It definitely gets me into trouble.\n\nDoctor: Have there been any times when the voices or beliefs were present only during your mood episodes and completely went away when your mood was back to normal?\n\nPatient: Well, no, it's not like they completely go away when my mood is normal. I told you, I still hear the guy in the vents even on my calm weeks. But... yeah, when my mood is all over the place, the voices and the signals are definitely there too. Like, when I get into those states where I'm only sleeping a couple of hours a night and I'm drawing up all these big master plans to completely reorganize the building's maintenance schedule... during those times, the vent voice is right there with me, and I feel absolutely sure the hallway lights flickering are sending out warnings about me. \n\nSpeaking of the hallway lights, they use these cheap fluorescent tubes now. The ballasts go bad all the time, and they just hum. It's this low, constant buzzing sound that drives you crazy if you stand under it too long. And they give off this awful greenish light that makes everybody look sick. I remember when buildings used to have real incandescent bulbs. They had that warm, yellow glow. Made things look cozy. My grandmother had this big floor lamp in her living room with a fringed shade. It was real heavy, made of brass, I think. She kept it right next to her reading chair. She used to read these thick romance novels, the ones with the painted covers where the guy always has his shirt ripped open. She'd get them by the dozen from the used bookstore downtown. That bookstore smelled like old paper and dust. They had a cat that just slept on the counter all day. A big orange tabby. I had an orange cat once, named Marmalade. He used to bring dead mice and leave them right on the welcome mat. You'd step out in the morning and nearly squish them. Mice are a huge problem in older buildings, you know. They get into the walls and chew through the wiring. That's a huge fire hazard. You have to put down traps, but the snap traps are messy, and the glue traps just seem cruel...\n\nBut yeah, when I'm all wired and making those big plans, the vent guy and the light warnings are definitely happening at the same time.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had hallucinations or delusional beliefs when you were not having a mood episode, such as a manic or depressive episode?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. Like I was saying before, there are plenty of times when I'm just... regular. You know? Not stuck in bed feeling depressed, and not all fired up and yelling at people. Just a normal, calm mood. But even during those calm stretches, for like two or three weeks at a time, I still hear the man in the vents plain as day. And I still know people in the building are signaling about me. \n\nIt's especially loud when I'm working near the main intake grates in the hallways. Those grates are massive. You wouldn't believe the amount of dust that gets sucked into those things. Management is supposed to order the good pleated filters, the thick ones, but they always cheap out and buy those flimsy blue fiberglass ones. They don't catch a damn thing. All the dust just blows right through the system and settles right back down on the baseboards. I swear I spend half my life wiping down baseboards. You can't just use a dry duster, either, or it just kicks the dirt right back into the air. You gotta use a damp rag. We used to use old cut-up t-shirts for rags when I was growing up. My mom kept a whole drawer of them under the kitchen counter. That drawer always got stuck in the summer when it was humid. The wood swells up, you know? You have to take a bar of soap and rub it along the wooden runners to make it glide smooth again. Plain old bar soap. Ivory works the best for that. Did you know Ivory soap floats? I dropped a bar in the bathtub when I was maybe eight years old, and it just bobbed right there on the top of the water. We only got to take real baths on Sunday nights before the school week started. You had to make sure you scrubbed behind your ears, or the teacher would send you to the nurse's office to get checked for lice...\n\nDoctor: Have the voices or beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?\n\nPatient: Yeah, like I was just saying, I have those calm stretches. I'll have those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high or deeply depressed, just... regular, you know? But yeah, it's definitely been for more than two weeks at a time during those calm periods where I still hear the man in the vents every single day, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just go away because my mood is normal. \n\nTwo weeks is a long time to deal with that. Actually, two weeks is exactly how long management made us wait for a new fan belt for the rooftop AC unit last August. Two whole weeks! You wouldn't believe how hot the top floor gets when the air goes out. It's like an oven up there. The tenants were complaining to me non-stop, leaving sticky notes on my utility cart. They think I can just magically fix it, but I don't carry commercial fan belts in my back pocket. You have to order those from a specialty supply house. \n\nAnd the supply houses aren't like they used to be, let me tell you. Used to be you could just drive down to the industrial park on 4th street and pick up whatever you needed. There was this guy there, Sal, who knew every part number by heart. He didn't even need to look at a computer. Computers ruin everything, if you ask me. Everything is automated now. You call a number and get a robot voice telling you to press one for sales, press two for service. My sister got locked out of her bank account last month because she couldn't get past the robot on the phone. She just wanted to check her balance, but it kept asking her for a PIN she forgot. She had to drive all the way down to the physical branch, and the parking there is an absolute nightmare. They have those tiny spots that barely fit a compact car, let alone her big station wagon. It's a real boat of a car, one of those old ones with the fake wood paneling on the side. You don't see cars like that anymore. Now they all look like jellybeans. Just round and silver or white. Nobody buys a green or a blue car anymore... \n\nBut yeah, even when my mood is totally fine for over two weeks, the vent guy is still talking and the signals are still happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you heard voices or believed people were sending you messages while you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?\n\nPatient: Didn't we... I think I just said that, didn't I? But yeah, yes. Like I was telling you, there have been those calmer weeks. Times when I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed, just... regular. But even then, for more than two weeks straight, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't stop just 'cause my mood is fine. \n\nTwo weeks... you know, speaking of two weeks, that's usually how long you have to wait to get any kind of doctor's appointment anywhere these days anyway. Actually, it's worse now. I tried to get in to see the dentist last month because my lower bridge was aching. Just a dull throb, right where the gum meets the metal. The receptionist—she had this bright purple hair, like, unnatural purple, like grape soda—she told me they couldn't see me until November. November! Who can wait that long with a toothache? I ended up just swishing warm salt water. Salt water fixes a lot of things. My granddad used to swear by it. He lived on the coast, out in Maine. Had this little dinghy he'd take out to check lobster traps. He smelled like brine and old tobacco. He used to smoke a pipe, the kind with a curved stem, always tapping it out on the heel of his boot... they don't make boots like they used to, either. Now the soles just peel right off if you step in a puddle.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices or beliefs ever been present only when you were feeling unusually high or irritable, and not at other times?\n\nPatient: Doc, are you pulling my leg? I feel like a broken record here. No, it's not just when I'm high or irritable. Like I keep trying to tell you, there have been those calmer weeks where I'm not especially high, and I'm not deeply depressed either. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks at a stretch, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still believe the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't only happen when my mood is all over the place. \n\nI really do feel like a broken record, though. You know, actual records are making a big comeback. I had to clear out apartment 4B a couple months ago after the tenant passed away, and his kids didn't want to deal with his stuff. Just left everything for me to deal with. He had all these plastic milk crates full of old vinyl records. Heavy as lead, let me tell you. I had to haul every single one of them down to the dumpster by myself. My lower back was screaming by the end of the shift. I tried going to one of those chiropractors once for my back, the guys that crack your neck? Scared the living daylights out of me. Sounded like a dry branch snapping in half. I prefer just using a heating pad now. I got one of those electric ones with the auto-shutoff timer, which is a lifesaver because I always fall asleep with it turned on. You really don't want to start a fire in the bed. Mattresses are basically kindling these days with all that memory foam stuff. It's just solid chemicals. Smells weird when you first take it out of the plastic wrapper, too. Like a chemical factory. You have to leave the windows open for days just to air the room out...\n\nDoctor: Have there ever been at least two weeks when you had the voices or beliefs like people were sending you messages, but you were not having any mood symptoms at all?\n\nPatient: Are you... wait, are you messing with me? Is this a test? Because I swear I've answered this exact same question like three times already. But yeah, yes, I'll say it again. There are those calmer weeks, right? Times when I'm not high, and I'm not deeply depressed. Just regular. But even then, for more than two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know the people in the building are signaling about me. \n\nIt's like talking to a brick wall here, Doc. Speaking of brick walls, the masonry on the east side of the building is starting to crumble. I noticed it last Tuesday when I was hosing down the sidewalk. The mortar is just turning to sand. I told the property manager, Mr. Henderson, but he just waved me off. He's always waving me off. He wears these cheap suits that look like they're made out of shiny plastic, and he always has a golf club in his office. Who plays golf in an office? It's ridiculous. He's got one of those little putting greens on the carpet. Carpet in an office is a terrible idea anyway. It just traps all the dirt and the coffee spills. You can never really get a coffee stain out of a light-colored carpet, no matter how much of that foaming spray you use. I've tried everything. Baking soda, vinegar, club soda... club soda works okay on blood, actually, if you get to it fast enough. Not that I clean up a lot of blood, but sometimes a tenant will cut their finger on a broken glass in the trash chute. People just throw loose glass down the chute! It's incredibly dangerous. I have to wear these thick leather gloves when I change the bins, the kind welders wear. They're stiff and you can barely bend your fingers, but it's better than getting sliced open. My buddy Tom got sliced open once, had to get twelve stitches...\n\nDoctor: Have there been any periods when the hallucinations or beliefs were present only during times you were depressed or manic, and not at other times?\n\nPatient: Doc, are we doing some kind of memory test? Because I'm starting to think you're the one who needs a checkup. I just... I literally just told you this. No, it's not only when I'm depressed or manic. I've had those calmer weeks, right? Weeks where I'm not high as a kite and I'm not down in the dumps. Just completely regular. But even then, for over two weeks, I still hear the man in the vents, and I still know for a fact the people in the building are signaling about me. It doesn't just happen when my mood is off. \n\nSpeaking of off, the thermostat in the lobby is completely shot. I've been telling Henderson for a month that it's stuck on 78 degrees. It's like a sauna down there. The poor ferns by the front desk are turning brown at the tips. You really have to mist ferns, you know? They like humidity, but not baking heat. My aunt had this massive Boston fern hanging on her porch. Thing was the size of a Volkswagen. She used to water it with leftover tea. Said the tannins were good for the soil. She drank a lot of tea, mostly that Earl Grey stuff. Smells like perfume to me. I prefer coffee. Black, no sugar. Sugar just rots your teeth anyway, which brings me right back to my lower bridge aching. I still haven't heard back from that purple-haired receptionist. You'd think she could at least put me on a cancellation list. People cancel dentist appointments all the time. Nobody actually wants to go to the dentist. They just go because they have to, like getting your car inspected. Speaking of cars, my registration is due next month, and the lines at the DMV... don't even get me started. You have to take a number and just sit there on those hard plastic chairs for hours. They always play the most depressing daytime TV on those little screens in the corner, too...\n\nDoctor: Have these voices or beliefs been going on, overall, for at least six months?\n\nPatient: Yeah, yeah, it's been way longer than six months. The voices and all that stuff with the people in the building... it's been going on for about a year and a half now. Ever since the winter before last. \n\nMan, that was a brutal winter, too. The pipes in the basement froze solid twice in one week. I was down there with a blowtorch and a space heater for hours trying to thaw them out before they burst. You ever see a cast iron pipe burst? It's like a bomb going off. Water everywhere, ruins everything. And the smell of stagnant water in a basement... it never really goes away. It gets into the concrete. You have to scrub it down with bleach, but then the whole building smells like a swimming pool for a month. I used to swim a lot when I was a kid. We had this public pool in my neighborhood, cost fifty cents to get in for the whole day. They had this high dive that felt like it was a hundred feet tall. I only jumped off it once, belly flopped so hard I thought I ruptured something. My chest was red for a week. I don't think they even build high dives at public pools anymore, too much liability. Everyone's so worried about getting sued these days. You can't even mop a floor without putting up six of those yellow caution signs, or someone will slip on purpose just to get a payout. I saw a guy do it once in the lobby, literally laid down on the wet tile and started groaning. I told Henderson to check the security tapes..."
